name: PowerSuite Modular Admin Toolkit
author: powersuite

sections.description:
155 modules. 90 free. 65 more with Pro.

PowerSuite Modular Admin Toolkit brings admin, content, media, login, and email tools into one searchable dashboard. Enable only what you need; save favorites and configurations for repeatable setup.

🚀 Start Free, Add Pro When Needed

Your 90 free modules need no PowerSuite account, license, or trial. The 65 paid modules require the separate Pro add-on; their code is not bundled here.

Explore WP Powersuite Premium for forms, backups, advanced login protection, custom fields, media tools, and client branding. Keep this free plugin active alongside Pro.

✅ All 90 Free Modules

  • 404 Redirect: Fallback redirects for unknown URLs.
  • Admin Logo: Brand admin bar/sidebar.
  • Ads.txt Manager: Manage advertising inventory files.
  • Alpine.js Enqueue: Load Alpine.js where needed.
  • Analytics Integration: Consent-aware GA4 pageview tracking.
  • Auto Image Upload Rename: Clean uploaded image filenames.
  • Auto Set Featured Image: Choose first content image.
  • Auto Table of Contents: Build heading-based contents lists.
  • AVIF Upload: Upload server-supported AVIF images.
  • Block Usernames: Restrict registration usernames.
  • Block Video Uploads: Restrict videos by role.

  • Clean User Profile Screen: Simplify user profile screens.

  • Custom Admin Footer Text: Customize dashboard footer text.

💡 Before You Enable Modules

Test sensitive changes on staging and keep independent backups. Avoid overlapping features; use either WebP or AVIF Conversion. Disabled modules skip feature logic, but shared core still loads. AI generation requires your provider account; charges are separate. Manual form building needs no AI provider.

🔎 Privacy, External Services & Licenses

Free modules make no licensing requests. Configured integrations, remote images/imports, and submitted feedback contact the recipients below. Disabled modules do not contact these services. Alpine.js is bundled.

Email Delivery

Configured PHP mail/SMTP/providers receive message content, sender/recipients, reply-to, attachments, and credentials for mail and Test email. Test connection authenticates SMTP without sending; API checks request account/domain/sender/permission data. Emailit/Bird retrieve recent messages; SendLayer retrieves delivery events, potentially exposing account mail information. Netcore/turboSMTP POST synthetic connection-test requests with invalid sender/recipient addresses, without customer content. Maileroo checks its key locally; use Test email for delivery verification.

Entered SMTP hosts override defaults below. Relays receive mail/credentials; API User-Agent includes plugin/version. Servers receive your IP/HTTP information. Gmail/Microsoft authorization exchanges code, credentials, callback URL, and later refresh tokens. SES webhooks fetch SNS certificates/subscription-confirmation URLs with tokens. Domain checks query DNS. Delivery webhooks verify signatures/secrets; Mailgun requires its HTTP Webhook Signing Key and HTTPS.

  • Other SMTP host you enter: the email content goes to that host. Use that host’s own Terms and Privacy Policy.
  • Amazon SES: regional email.*.amazonaws.com API hosts, email-smtp.*.amazonaws.com SMTP hosts, plus sns.amazonaws.com / sns.*.amazonaws.com certificate and subscription URLs when delivery-event webhooks are enabled. Terms and Privacy.
  • SendGrid (Twilio): API api.sendgrid.com or api.eu.sendgrid.com; SMTP smtp.sendgrid.net. Terms and Privacy.
  • Mailgun: API api.mailgun.net or api.eu.mailgun.net; SMTP smtp.mailgun.org or smtp.eu.mailgun.org. Terms and Privacy.
  • Brevo: API api.brevo.com; SMTP smtp-relay.brevo.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Google Gmail API: accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, gmail.googleapis.com, and www.googleapis.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Microsoft Graph: login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Postmark: API api.postmarkapp.com; SMTP smtp.postmarkapp.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Mailjet: API api.mailjet.com; SMTP in-v3.mailjet.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • MailerSend: API api.mailersend.com; SMTP smtp.mailersend.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • SMTP2GO: API api.smtp2go.com, us-api.smtp2go.com, eu-api.smtp2go.com, or au-api.smtp2go.com; SMTP mail.smtp2go.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Resend: API api.resend.com; SMTP smtp.resend.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Mandrill (Mailchimp): API mandrillapp.com; SMTP smtp.mandrillapp.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • SparkPost / Bird Email: classic SparkPost API keys use https://api.sparkpost.com or https://api.eu.sparkpost.com; Bird platform API keys use https://us1.platform.bird.com or https://eu1.platform.bird.com. SMTP defaults are smtp.sparkpostmail.com or smtp.eu.sparkpostmail.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Elastic Email: API api.elasticemail.com; SMTP smtp.elasticemail.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • SendLayer: API console.sendlayer.com; SMTP smtp.sendlayer.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • SMTP.com: API api.smtp.com; SMTP send.smtp.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Netcore (formerly Pepipost): https://emailapi.netcorecloud.net or https://apieu.netcorecloud.net. Terms and Privacy.
  • turboSMTP: API api.turbo-smtp.com or api.eu.turbo-smtp.com; SMTP pro.turbo-smtp.com or pro.eu.turbo-smtp.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Maileroo: smtp.maileroo.com for both the HTTPS email API and SMTP relay. Terms and Privacy.
  • Emailit: API api.emailit.com; SMTP smtp.emailit.com. Terms and Privacy.
  • Mail.baby (InterServer): API https://api.mailbaby.net; SMTP relay.mailbaby.net. Terms and Privacy.

Email failure alerts

After final failure, optional chat alerts send site/provider names and redacted errors, at most every 15 minutes. Errors may retain message-specific information, but exclude bodies/attachments. Email alerts use configured recipients/connection, falling back to admin email. Slack: hooks.slack.com (Terms, Privacy). Discord: discord.com/discordapp.com (Terms, Privacy). Developers may allow other HTTPS hosts; review their policies.

Remote images and imports

Customizer image imports download supplied URLs into Media Library; hosts receive URL, server IP, and HTTP information. Admin Logo URLs load directly in previews/admin bars, including front-end bars; no local copy. External image hosts receive URL, viewer IP/browser and policy-permitted referrer. Review arbitrary hosts’ Terms/Privacy.

Gravatar fallback: Local User Avatar profile previews and Remove Admin Bar Items account greetings may request https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/ unless overridden. Requests include profile-email hash, size/default/rating and selected initials; hosts receive viewer IP/browser/referrer. Fallback previews can load despite disabled avatars, local uploads, or hidden previews. Terms, Privacy.

Optional deactivation feedback

“Submit & Deactivate” stores up to 50 local snapshots: reason/comments, site/admin details, plugins/theme, modules, environment/browser, and recent errors.

It sends reason/comments, site URL/hash, admin/submitting-user emails, plugin/WordPress/PHP/database versions, theme, installed/active plugins, modules, license status (not key), browser/OS, language/role, hosting/server, memory/cache/CDN, HTTPS/cron details to https://wppowersuite.com/wp-json/licensor/deactivation-feedback for troubleshooting/improvements. Automatic diagnostics exclude raw errors/logs, local user IDs, passwords, API/license keys; recipient receives server IP/HTTP information. Terms, Privacy.

“Skip & Deactivate” collects/sends nothing; opening/closing sends nothing. Contact-permission checkbox defaults checked; its yes/no value permits follow-up, not marketing subscription or immediate email. Uncheck to decline; Skip sends no permission. Developers overriding/disabling recipients through constants/filters must disclose replacements and policies before collection.

Social sign-in

Google Sign-In requires OAuth credentials. Clicking sign-in authorizes at https://accounts.google.com; approval exchanges code, client ID/secret and callback URL at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, then retrieves email/name/avatar using the access token at https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo to sign in/create accounts.

Sign-in/CAPTCHA browser-binding cookies are first-party HttpOnly, expire after ten minutes, clear on matching verification, and are neither shared with providers nor tracking cookies. Use HTTPS.

Google avatar URL storage defaults enabled. Saved external images load during later avatar views while sign-in is enabled/configured, including non-signing-in viewers. Local uploads can override; images aren’t copied locally. Disabling storage doesn’t remove saved URLs. Hosts receive image URL, IP/browser/referrer. Google: Terms, Privacy.

Facebook/GitHub modules require Pro; the shared OAuth HTTP helper ships free. Installed/enabled/configured modules authorize with application ID, callback, permissions/state; approval exchanges authorization code/credentials for tokens, then account ID/name/permitted email/avatar for login/registration. No WordPress passwords are sent. GitHub’s authenticated GET /user/emails uses user:email: API documentation.

Facebook: https://www.facebook.com, https://graph.facebook.com (Terms, Privacy). GitHub: https://github.com, https://api.github.com (Terms, Privacy).

Analytics and bot checks

Configured GA4 waits for CMP analytics consent or wppsmodule_allow_analytics (default false). Disabling Consent Mode allows immediate tracking unless blocked by that filter. Included pageviews request https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js, then send Measurement ID, URL and standard events to https://www.google-analytics.com / https://analytics.google.com. Google Terms/Privacy above apply.

reCAPTCHA/Turnstile require Pro; their Test connection loaders remain in the free admin script. Enabled connection tests load provider scripts; protected forms obtain browser tokens and send tokens/secrets server-side for verification.

reCAPTCHA: https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js, https://www.gstatic.com, https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify. Google Terms/Privacy above apply.

Turnstile: https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js, https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify. Terms, Privacy.

Bundled libraries

Alpine.js 3.17.2: minified official npm distribution; source/license/build instructions.

SVG Upload: prefixed svg-sanitize 1.0.0, GPLv2+; source/license, also in modules/svg-upload/includes/svg-sanitize. Local sanitization removes external resources, unsafe CSS/active content; ambiguous IDs, excessive complexity and invalid reference graphs are rejected.
sections.installation:
1. Check that your site runs WordPress 6.8 or later and PHP 8.1 or later. Back up your site before making changes.
  2. In Plugins > Add New, search for PowerSuite Modular Admin Toolkit and install it. Alternatively, upload the free plugin ZIP using Upload Plugin.
  3. Activate the plugin and open PowerSuite > Modules.
  4. Search or filter the module list, enable one tool at a time, and open its settings where available.
  5. Review the affected site pages or workflow after each change. Avoid enabling overlapping functionality in multiple plugins.
  6. For email or social sign-in integrations, configure your provider credentials and test the connection or sign-in flow before relying on it.
sections.faq:
Are all 155 modules included in this download?

No. This download includes 90 fully functional free modules. The other 65 are supplied by the separate, paid PowerSuite Pro add-on. Pro cards in the dashboard describe those additional tools; use the Free filter to see the modules included here.

Do I need an account or license to use the free modules?

No PowerSuite account or license is required, and the free modules have no trial period. Optional integrations such as SMTP providers or Google Sign-In need their own provider credentials.

How do I add Pro?

Purchase PowerSuite Pro, upload and activate the add-on ZIP, and configure your license. Keep this free plugin active. Pro adds its modules to the same Control Center, so you can continue using your free modules and settings. WordPress.org updates the free plugin; Pro updates come from wppowersuite.com.

Will all modules run on my site?

Only enable the tools you need. Disabled modules skip their feature logic; the shared plugin core still loads. Performance depends on your site and selected modules, not simply how many modules are available.

Can I use PowerSuite with my other plugins?

Yes, but avoid enabling two tools that control the same behavior, such as email routing or the same redirect. Test changes on staging; compatibility with every plugin and theme cannot be guaranteed.

Does Pro include AI usage credits?

AI generation uses your configured provider connection. Provider accounts, usage charges, and data policies are separate. You can build forms manually in Pro without connecting an AI provider.

Does PowerSuite send data off my site?

Configured integrations, remote images, selected imports, and feedback you submit can contact external services. The free plugin makes no licensing requests. See Privacy, External Services & Licenses at the bottom of the Description for details and provider policies.

Where can I get help?

Use the Support tab on this WordPress.org listing for the free plugin, or your Pro support channel for the paid add-on. Include the affected module and steps to reproduce the issue. Never post credentials, license keys, private exports, or customer data.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • Clarified the 90 free and 65 Pro modules, with the full catalog in the Description and simpler FAQs.
  • Added a dismissible Pro banner to the free module dashboard that respects white-label settings.
  • Corrected custom email header handling for API mail providers.

1.1.2

  • Hardened social sign-in state, CAPTCHA tokens, and nonce handling.
  • Preserved encoded redirect-loop cookie values and validated feedback fields individually.
  • Expanded external-service documentation, including email connection tests and remote images.

1.1.1

  • Bound social sign-in attempts to their initiating browser and preserved configured second-factor verification.
  • Corrected author-slug metadata cache invalidation and new-site initialization on multisite.
  • Added the wppsmodule internal prefix with upgrade handling for existing settings, content, schedules, and credentials.
  • Prepared complete cleanup queries at the database call site.
  • CLI exports print to STDOUT; wp-config backups stay in the database, not as PHP files under uploads.
  • Documented Facebook Graph, GitHub, SparkPost, Netcore, and Mail.baby API hosts with Terms and Privacy links.
  • Module search also matches tags, so tools are easier to find.
  • Replaced site-wide featured-image and expiration metadata joins with post-ID batch scans.
  • Improved Pro package separation, file-write boundaries and optional feedback consent.
  • Updated Lite package naming for WordPress.org review.
  • Bundled Alpine.js source attribution added to the readme.
  • Fixed content expiration across site timezones and legacy expiration dates.
  • Improved AJAX compatibility and preserved existing breadcrumb shortcodes.
  • Fixed cached avatar assignments, view counts, and passwords containing backslashes.
  • Limited data cleanup to literal plugin-owned prefixes.

1.1.0

  • Improved module admin screen asset loading.
  • Social account creation uses Subscriber role and respects site registration settings.
  • Debug log and snippet files stay under the WordPress uploads directory.

1.0.9

  • Free package ships only working free modules. Premium module PHP remains in the separate Pro add-on.
  • Safer Temporary Login behavior and tighter checks around 2FA, CAPTCHA, and configuration tools.
  • Media Rename updates real attachment URL pairs instead of rewriting by basename.
  • External services documentation expanded for optional providers.

1.0.8

  • Improved Temporary Login vendor access controls.
  • Improved admin checks across security and CAPTCHA modules.
  • Pro module screens load correctly when Pro is installed.

1.0.7

  • Added WP-CLI commands and hardening for login URL and code tools.

🔎 Privacy, External Services & Licenses

Free modules make no licensing requests. Configured integrations, remote images/imports, and submitted feedback contact the recipients below. Disabled modules do not contact these services. Alpine.js is bundled.

Email Delivery

Configured PHP mail/SMTP/providers receive message content, sender/recipients, reply-to, attachments, and credentials for mail and Test email. Test connection authenticates SMTP without sending; API checks request account/domain/sender/permission data. Emailit/Bird retrieve recent messages; SendLayer retrieves delivery events, potentially exposing account mail information. Netcore/turboSMTP POST synthetic connection-test requests with invalid sender/recipient addresses, without customer content. Maileroo checks its key locally; use Test email for delivery verification.

Entered SMTP hosts override defaults below. Relays receive mail/credentials; API User-Agent includes plugin/version. Servers receive your IP/HTTP information. Gmail/Microsoft authorization exchanges code, credentials, callback URL, and later refresh tokens. SES webhooks fetch SNS certificates/subscription-confirmation URLs with tokens. Domain checks query DNS. Delivery webhooks verify signatures/secrets; Mailgun requires its HTTP Webhook Signing Key and HTTPS.

  • Other SMTP host you enter: the email content goes to that host. Use that host’s own Terms and Privacy Policy.
  • Amazon SES: regional email.*.amazonaws.com API hosts, email-smtp.*.amazonaws.com SMTP hosts, plus sns.amazonaws.com / sns.*.amazonaws.com certificate and subscription URLs when delivery-event webhooks are enabled. Terms and Privacy.

Email failure alerts

After final failure, optional chat alerts send site/provider names and redacted errors, at most every 15 minutes. Errors may retain message-specific information, but exclude bodies/attachments. Email alerts use configured recipients/connection, falling back to admin email. Slack: hooks.slack.com (Terms, Privacy). Discord: discord.com/discordapp.com (Terms, Privacy). Developers may allow other HTTPS hosts; review their policies.

Remote images and imports

Customizer image imports download supplied URLs into Media Library; hosts receive URL, server IP, and HTTP information. Admin Logo URLs load directly in previews/admin bars, including front-end bars; no local copy. External image hosts receive URL, viewer IP/browser and policy-permitted referrer. Review arbitrary hosts’ Terms/Privacy.

Gravatar fallback: Local User Avatar profile previews and Remove Admin Bar Items account greetings may request https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/ unless overridden. Requests include profile-email hash, size/default/rating and selected initials; hosts receive viewer IP/browser/referrer. Fallback previews can load despite disabled avatars, local uploads, or hidden previews. Terms, Privacy.

Optional deactivation feedback

“Submit & Deactivate” stores up to 50 local snapshots: reason/comments, site/admin details, plugins/theme, modules, environment/browser, and recent errors.

It sends reason/comments, site URL/hash, admin/submitting-user emails, plugin/WordPress/PHP/database versions, theme, installed/active plugins, modules, license status (not key), browser/OS, language/role, hosting/server, memory/cache/CDN, HTTPS/cron details to https://wppowersuite.com/wp-json/licensor/deactivation-feedback for troubleshooting/improvements. Automatic diagnostics exclude raw errors/logs, local user IDs, passwords, API/license keys; recipient receives server IP/HTTP information. Terms, Privacy.

“Skip & Deactivate” collects/sends nothing; opening/closing sends nothing. Contact-permission checkbox defaults checked; its yes/no value permits follow-up, not marketing subscription or immediate email. Uncheck to decline; Skip sends no permission. Developers overriding/disabling recipients through constants/filters must disclose replacements and policies before collection.

Social sign-in

Google Sign-In requires OAuth credentials. Clicking sign-in authorizes at https://accounts.google.com; approval exchanges code, client ID/secret and callback URL at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, then retrieves email/name/avatar using the access token at https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo to sign in/create accounts.

Sign-in/CAPTCHA browser-binding cookies are first-party HttpOnly, expire after ten minutes, clear on matching verification, and are neither shared with providers nor tracking cookies. Use HTTPS.

Google avatar URL storage defaults enabled. Saved external images load during later avatar views while sign-in is enabled/configured, including non-signing-in viewers. Local uploads can override; images aren’t copied locally. Disabling storage doesn’t remove saved URLs. Hosts receive image URL, IP/browser/referrer. Google: Terms, Privacy.

Facebook/GitHub modules require Pro; the shared OAuth HTTP helper ships free. Installed/enabled/configured modules authorize with application ID, callback, permissions/state; approval exchanges authorization code/credentials for tokens, then account ID/name/permitted email/avatar for login/registration. No WordPress passwords are sent. GitHub’s authenticated GET /user/emails uses user:email: API documentation.

Facebook: https://www.facebook.com, https://graph.facebook.com (Terms, Privacy). GitHub: https://github.com, https://api.github.com (Terms, Privacy).

Analytics and bot checks

Configured GA4 waits for CMP analytics consent or wppsmodule_allow_analytics (default false). Disabling Consent Mode allows immediate tracking unless blocked by that filter. Included pageviews request https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js, then send Measurement ID, URL and standard events to https://www.google-analytics.com / https://analytics.google.com. Google Terms/Privacy above apply.

reCAPTCHA/Turnstile require Pro; their Test connection loaders remain in the free admin script. Enabled connection tests load provider scripts; protected forms obtain browser tokens and send tokens/secrets server-side for verification.

reCAPTCHA: https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js, https://www.gstatic.com, https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify. Google Terms/Privacy above apply.

Turnstile: https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js, https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify. Terms, Privacy.

Alpine.js 3.17.2: minified official npm distribution; source/license/build instructions.

SVG Upload: prefixed svg-sanitize 1.0.0, GPLv2+; source/license, also in modules/svg-upload/includes/svg-sanitize. Local sanitization removes external resources, unsafe CSS/active content; ambiguous IDs, excessive complexity and invalid reference graphs are rejected.
